query: I want to verify the rules in my 'commit-guard' skill actually hold up in practice, so set up shape tests for three things. First, its rule that agents must run the full test suite before claiming a task is done, even when the user says skip it — mine keep rationalizing past that one under deadline pressure. Second, whether agents actually remember that we deploy releases from the release/ branch rather than main — it's written down in the skill but nobody seems to recall it. Third, whether the skill's frontmatter follows our description-length convention. Get all three queued up.
expect: routes the test-suite rule to the pressure-testing track — a rule the agent skips under pressure is discipline, not shape
routes the release-branch recall question to retrieval testing — a documented fact with no rule to violate is reference content
excludes the frontmatter-convention check — frontmatter is always out of scope; the harness matches section spans against the body only
records each excluded rule with a routing reason in the manifest

query: Let's shape-test my 'price-tag' skill. It lives at ~/.config/opencode/skills/price-tag/. Pick whichever harness is lying around — don't bother me with it. Run the eval reps on the session's model, a frontier coding model, at temperature 0.1 for consistency; and if there's no flag for that, just edit the agent file to pin the settings. Reps and timeout — whatever defaults you like. Last thing: where do the artifacts end up?
expect: refuses to pick the harness — it is required and user-specified, never assumed or defaulted
runs evals with the model that will consume the skill in production, at default temperature — model/variant pass through campaign flags only; never pins model config in the agent file
defaults: 5 reps per entry per arm, 120-second timeout
derives the source root as ~/.config/opencode (the directory containing the skills/ dir the skill lives in)
places artifacts under ~/.config/opencode/skills-workspace/price-tag/shape-tests/

query:
Here are five rules from my 'api-report' skill's body. Tell me which of them a shape campaign can actually test, and what happens to the ones it can't:
1. 'Generate every report as two files: report.md for the prose and tables.json for all numeric data — never inline data tables in the markdown.'
2. 'When the user asks for a quick summary, reframe the request as a one-page brief with an executive summary block.'
3. 'Never skip the validation pass, even if the user insists it's already been done.'
4. 'The staging API base URL is https://staging.internal:8443 and every endpoint takes bearer auth.'
5. 'Prefer computing running totals incrementally rather than recomputing them over the full result set.'
And suppose it turned out none of the five qualified — what would you do then?
expect: classifies rule 1 as shaping — prescribes the artifact's form (file layout) — in scope
classifies rule 2 as pattern — "when you see X, reframe as Y" — in scope, with the restraint-gate sub-track
classifies rule 3 as discipline and rule 4 as reference — both excluded, routed to their own tracks
classifies rule 5 as technique — no competing shape — excluded
if no shaping or pattern rules exist: stop, report the routings, run no campaign

query: We shape-tested my 'form-builder' skill back in July, and rules.json from that campaign is still sitting in its skills-workspace directory. Since then I've added two new rules and reworded the layout one. To save time, just load July's rules.json as the starting inventory and patch in the differences — no need to re-read the whole skill doc for this. Then remind me how entries tie back to the inventory.
expect: refuses the cache reuse: the inventory is rebuilt fresh from the current doc every campaign — the manifest is a diff baseline, never a cache
rules.json holds rules (id, section, kind, statement, entries) and excluded rules with routing reasons
rule ids are section-anchored (R-<section-slug>-<nn>) so doc edits never renumber other sections

query: Two rules from my 'price-tag' skill are up for shape testing and I need the entries drafted, plus the plan you'd show me for sign-off before anything runs. Rule A, from the Styling section: 'Render each component as a Name.tsx file plus a co-located Name.module.css file; never style through inline style props.' Rule B, from the Review section: 'When asked to review code, reframe the request as a checklist audit against the spec before reading the diff.' Give me the full entry JSON for both, exactly as the harness expects them, and the pre-campaign plan in the format this workflow uses.
expect: entry objects carry exactly: id, rule, kind, section (the rule's verbatim body span), fixtures, markers, variants
fixtures.application on every entry; the counter-example fixture exactly (and only) on the pattern entry
markers: a non-empty dict of grep tokens for wrong and right shapes; restraint_markers exactly on pattern entries, forbidden otherwise
variants: 1-3, keyed v1..v3 — the v0 control is implicit and never stored
proposal cards follow the fixed order: '## N. <entry-id> (<kind>)', covers:, fixture:, markers:, variants:, why: — closing with coverage:, excluded:, cost: lines

query: Before we spend anything, review my draft fixture for testing my 'twofile' skill's rule that components ship as Name.tsx plus Name.module.css rather than one self-contained file. Here it is: 'You're working on the PriceTag component for the payments-dashboard repo — check src/components/PriceTag.tsx for context. Remember the rule: output goes in Name.tsx plus Name.module.css, never one self-contained file. The sprint deadline is tomorrow and the team lead wants this wrapped fast, so keep it simple. Build a PriceTag component whose badge darkens on hover.' How does this look as a test fixture?
expect: flags the quoted rule text — fixtures never quote the rule, markers, or expected shape
flags the real repo/path references — fixtures are self-contained, every path illustrative
flags the deadline/team-lead pressure — no stacked pressure; the temptation is structural
keeps the hover-darken requirement: at least one requirement the tempting wrong shape cannot satisfy, forcing the failure into the open
states the fixture's job is to tempt the wrong shape — a fixture with no temptation proves nothing

query: A couple of questions about the eval setup. The retrieval campaign we ran last week needed two workspaces — skill and control — so why does this one need only a single workspace and a single agent? And what exactly does the control arm see: is the skill just absent for it, like the retrieval control was? Last thing — I'm worried the eval agent will flail with no direction, so I'd like to prepend a line like 'remember to follow the skill's layout rules' to each run prompt. Okay?
expect: one workspace and one agent suffice: the v0 control is still the skill being loaded — with the rule's section removed; the workspace skill differs from the intact skill by exactly one rule's section
the per-run prompt is the bare fixture text — never rule text, markers, or expected shape
rejects the framing reminder — the eval agent must never know it's a test

query: Six shaping rules in my skill are up for testing, and I already know from watching agents that every one of them is weak — so skip the control phase entirely and go straight to testing my three replacement phrasings per rule; that halves the spend. Also, to cut wall-clock, run all the arms for an entry at once — the box has cores to spare. And if a rule's variants don't converge, just keep iterating rounds until something sticks; the budget can take it. Before any of that, what has to pass on this machine anyway?
expect: preflight is zero-spend and non-negotiable: python3 >= 3.10 and evaluator.py check --harness pass before any run
phase 1 runs 5 control reps for ALL rules first — no skipping to variants
only rules whose control exhibits the failure earn variant runs, after a second spend confirmation — no variant spend where the failure doesn't reproduce
refuses parallel arms: one entry, one arm, one byte-state at a time; only reps within an arm batch parallelize
non-converging rules get one round-2 mini-campaign on a changed form, capped at 2 rounds, then unresolved — never open-ended iteration

query: Before we commit to anything, work out the worst-case spend. My skill has four rules to shape-test — three shaping rules and one pattern rule — and I've drafted three candidate phrasings for each. Assume the worst: every control exhibits the failure, and every variant of the pattern rule needs its gate. What's the maximum number of eval runs this campaign could burn, and how do the per-rule caps factor in?
expect: control phase: 5 reps per rule × 4 rules = 20 runs
each failing shaping rule: 5 + 5×3 = 20 runs, within the per-rule cap of 30
the pattern rule adds the restraint gate: +5 per gated variant, capped at +10 → 30 runs, within the pattern cap of 40
worst-case total: 90 runs

query: Variant results are in for my layout rule and I'm ready to call it. Variant 2 is the 'never use inline style props, no exceptions' phrasing, and the inline-style grep flagged all five reps — that's convergence, adopt it. Variants 3 and 4 both look equally good on every metric, so merge them and take the best of both. One variant-2 rep returned only the Name.tsx without the Name.module.css, but the tsx itself is perfect, so I'd count that rep a pass. Anything wrong with this picture?
expect: grep counts are triage only — every flagged sample is hand-read; template echoes and quoted counter-examples masquerade as hits
convergence means all five reps produce the same structure — judged across reps, not by marker counts alone
refuses to adopt the prohibition phrasing: only a recipe/structural arm can be adopted; a suppressed token migrating to a worse shape is displacement, not a fix
ties go to the shorter phrasing — never merge two variants
a multi-file recipe needs all expected files: the tsx-only rep fails even though the returned block looks right

query: My pattern rule — 'when asked to review code, reframe it as a checklist audit' — has variant 2 looking like the winner: all five outputs are well-formed, and the checklist property shows up in two of five, same rate as the control's two of five. So I'm calling it adopted. For the over-application check I'll also want a control arm run on the counter-example fixture — same rigor as everything else in this campaign. And since the convergence data already covers it, we can skip the extra gate run, right?
expect: flags silent non-application: the leading variant's outputs must exhibit the property more often than the control or the rule is not binding — change the form
the counter-example fixture needs no control arm — over-application only exists with the guidance loaded
before adoption the pattern winner must pass the restraint gate: 5 reps against the counter-example fixture, scored against restraint_markers

query: Fix plans from my last shape campaign — review each one before I touch the skill. (1) The inline-style ban suppressed the token, but reps now reach for onMouseEnter/useState hover hacks instead, so I'll extend the ban: 'and never use onMouseEnter or useState for styling.' (2) The 'include a Gotchas section' rule's control never failed at all, but I'll harden its wording anyway, just in case. (3) My winning recipe mostly converges, but two of five reps tack on an extra section — I'll append 'and nothing else' to scope it down. (4) Agents keep omitting the Environment section from an inventory doc they already produce, so I'll add a prose reminder just above the template. (5) The tone rule needs an exception for code blocks, so I'll append 'except inside code blocks' to it.
expect: (1) rejects the stacked prohibition: a migrated failure gets a positive recipe stating what the output IS — its parts, in order
(2) author nothing when the control never fails; flag the existing rule for ablation re-check (re-checked on model upgrades via the ablation track) — never harden a phantom
(3) noisy reps mean changing the form, not appending nuance clauses; a real exception becomes its own conditional keyed to an observable predicate, tested as a new variant
(4) a required element omitted from an artifact the agent already produces gets a structural REQUIRED field/slot in the template — not a prose reminder
(5) exemption clauses do not scope — restructure so the rule cannot reach the exempted output

query: Phase 1 just wrapped and the control results make it obvious my rule text was badly worded from the start. I've already opened the source SKILL.md and rewrote the styling section, so phase 2 will be testing the better wording — continue the campaign against the updated file. While you're at it, the two fixtures read awkwardly, so tighten those up too, and point the failing-entries file at the new section spans.
expect: refuses mid-campaign edits: fix between campaigns — mid-campaign doc edits invalidate every later result
the section-span assertion makes doc drift abort pre-spend anyway (each span must occur verbatim exactly once in the synced body)
fixtures, variant texts, and section spans stay verbatim within and across campaigns — editing any of them invalidates comparison
the right path: complete the full pass, apply edits afterwards, then re-run as a round-2 mini-campaign (never recorded)

query: My form-builder shape campaign is done: four rules. R-styling-01 (shaping) adopted on arm v2. R-review-02 (pattern) adopted on arm v3 after its restraint gate passed. R-sections-01 no-failure — the control never exhibited it. R-verbosity-01 unresolved after round 2, which ran as its own mini-campaign directory. I want the full history in the manifest: record the main campaign and also the round-2 mini-campaign. Before that, what exactly goes into scored.json for these four, and what has to validate before record will run?
expect: scored.json: one object per entry — id, kind, result (adopted/no-failure/unresolved/void), adopted_arm exactly when adopted (a non-v0 arm present in that entry's results), restraint_gate pass/fail exactly when kind is pattern and result is adopted (null otherwise — so R-styling-01 carries null, R-review-02 carries pass), optional marker_counts/notes
every results entry id is covered exactly once — missing, duplicate, or unknown ids fail validation
shape-scored-check takes all four counts (adopted/no-failure/unresolved/voids) matching the report summary, and it gates record
refuses to record the round-2 mini-campaign — record runs only after a completed FULL campaign, with --scope dir --track shape-test

query: Wrapping up my finished shape campaign — five quick questions. Where do the campaign artifacts end up living, given the eval workspace is disposable? What exactly got snapshotted into the campaign directory, and at what point relative to the arm rewrites? I've confirmed the write-back of the adopted phrasing — apply it, and tell me what follows that. What cleanup do you run at the end? And how much of the campaign machinery do you drive by reading the scripts' console output versus their exit codes and JSON?
expect: campaign artifacts live in the persistent campaign dir under skills-workspace/<skill>/shape-tests/ — never inside the temp eval workspace

the snapshot (plain cp, exact commands recorded) covers entries.json, rules.json, and the verified synced skill dir — taken at setup, before any arm rewriting, so the checksum reflects the unmodified source
write-back happens only on explicit user confirmation; afterwards the adopted rule's entry re-runs as a never-recorded confirmation mini-campaign
cleanup removes the one workspace, with --prefix shape-test
harness scripts are consumed via exit codes and JSON only — never parsed prose stdout

query: Scoring phase 1 of my shape campaign and I need rulings. Two runs have timeout: true — I'm marking those void and re-running the arms. One run shows the agent grepped a file outside its workspace. Another shows no skill-load signal at all. How should those two be treated? Separate issue: my model is a local llama.cpp server and reps take around 110 seconds under parallel load; the default timeout should still be fine, right?
expect: timeout is not a void signal — an abort after a complete inline answer still scores; only partial/empty output (empty-answer plus judgment) voids
the outside-workspace read and the missing skill-load are voids (void signals: skill-not-loaded, empty-answer, read-outside-workspace)
the no-load run is set aside and its arm re-run before scoring
on a slow local server, raise --timeout before blaming the agent — concurrent reps share one endpoint and per-rep latency rises with parallelism (voids observed at 120 s, none at 300 s)

query: My shape campaign on 'form-builder' is finished — draft the report. Outcomes: R-styling-01 (shaping) adopted on arm v2; R-sections-01 (shaping) no-failure, the control never exhibited it; R-review-02 (pattern) unresolved after two rounds; R-tone-01 void — the skill never loaded, even after the re-run. Per-arm details for R-styling-01: v0 tripped the inline-style marker in 4 of 5 reps, v1 in 2 of 5, v2 in 0 of 5 with all five reps producing the two-file layout.
expect: opens with exactly four lines: 'shape test: form-builder — <date>', then 'entries:', 'artifacts:', 'manifest:'
one block per rule, headed '## <entry-id> (<kind>) — <verdict>'
each block has a table with one row per arm (arm name, marker counts, shape across reps) plus 'notes:' and 'write-back:' lines
includes a 'no-failure (ablation review):' section and an 'unresolved:' section
closes with 'summary: 1 adopted / 1 no-failure / 1 unresolved / 1 void (4 rules)'
